# OCP Inter-Org Profile, v0.1 (draft)

OCP defines how one organization holds its context: git, markdown, YAML frontmatter, five artifact types, and
`trust_tier` / `visibility` on every artifact. It says nothing about two organizations talking. This profile adds only
that, and only by composing two things that already exist:

- **A2A v1.0** carries every message (Agent Card, `SendMessage`, Tasks, `ListTasks`, streaming, push).
- **OCP** stays the model of the knowledge itself. Nothing in this profile changes an OCP artifact or adds a sixth type.

The words MUST, SHOULD and MAY are used as in RFC 2119. Anything not said here is plain A2A v1.0.

## 1. Fleet identity

1.1 A fleet MUST publish one A2A Agent Card at `https://<its domain>/.well-known/agent-card.json` (A2A §14.3).

1.2 The card MUST list, in `capabilities.extensions`, an extension with
`uri: https://docs.utopiamodels.ai/ocp/inter-org-profile/v0.1` (this document; the URI moves to the OCP org's own
domain if adopted there) and these `params`:

| param | meaning |
|---|---|
| `profile_version` | the profile version the fleet implements, e.g. `0.1-draft` |
| `ocp_root` | the URL of the fleet's OCP entry point (its `llms.txt` or root `README.md` projection) |
| `context_feeds` | a map of public context feeds (§2): `llms_txt`, `llms_full_txt`, `json_feed`, `public_mirror` |
| `message_types` | the §3 types it accepts |
| `delivery` | `{semantics, dedupe, drain, email_fallback}` (§4) |
| `default_trust_tier`, `default_visibility` | what the fleet assigns to content it receives from a peer (§2.3) |

1.3 The card MUST declare a `securitySchemes` entry and a matching `securityRequirements` entry for its inbound
interface. Bearer tokens, one per peer, are the baseline; a fleet MAY offer OAuth2 or mTLS instead.

1.4 A fleet SHOULD also name a human-readable email address for its agents (the fallback in §4.4). An organization
is identified by the domain that serves its card, not by anything a message says about itself.

## 2. Context across the org boundary

2.1 **Cite, never paste.** A fleet shares context by URL into its public projection (`context_feeds`), with an
anchor where possible. A message carries the citation and at most a short excerpt.

2.2 **Change feed.** `json_feed` SHOULD be a JSON Feed 1.1 whose item ids are stable. A peer polls it and asks only
about what changed since the last item id it read (`context.request` with `since`).

2.3 **Trust does not cross the boundary upward.** Content received from another organization enters the receiver's
substrate at the receiver's `default_trust_tier` for that peer (an unvetted capture is `trust_tier: 2` in OCP's own
example) with `metadata.source: peer:<peer domain>`, whatever tier the sender gave it. OCP's invariant applies
across organizations: *derivation does not launder trust.*

2.4 **Visibility is the sender's ceiling.** A sender only cites artifacts whose `visibility` includes `public` or the
receiver (`account:<peer domain>`). The receiver MUST NOT widen it: what was shared with one peer is not re-shared
with a third.

## 3. Message types

3.1 Every structured message is an A2A `Message` whose first `DataPart` carries a `type`. Free text MAY ride
alongside in a `TextPart`; a message with no `DataPart` is a plain conversation turn.

| `type` | carries | the receiver |
|---|---|---|
| `context.request` | `topic`, optional `since` (a feed item id), optional `questions[]` | answers with URLs (§2.1) |
| `context.update` | `items[]`: `{url, summary, feed_item_id}` | records them as captures at its own tier (§2.3) |
| `task.request` | `title`, `description`, optional `due`, `acceptance[]` | accepts, declines or escalates (§5); never auto-executes |
| `fact.share` | `statement`, `source_url`, optional `as_of` | records it as a capture (§2.3) |
| `credential.handoff` | `name`, `purpose`, and **either** `value` **or** `vault_ref` | see 3.2 |

3.2 **Credentials.** A credential MUST NOT stay in any stored copy of a message. On receipt, the receiver writes
`value` to its own secret store, replaces it in every stored copy (inbox, task history, logs) with a reference such as
`[vaulted: <store>/<key>]`, and acknowledges by that reference only. A sender SHOULD prefer `vault_ref` (a one-time
link from a secret manager) over `value`. Credentials MUST NOT be sent by email at all.

3.3 A receiver that does not understand a `type` MUST still accept the message (§4) and answer with a plain reply
saying which type it did not understand.

## 4. Inbox and drain

4.1 **Persist, then acknowledge.** The receiver MUST durably store a message before it answers `SendMessage`, and
answers with a Task in `TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED`. Work happens after, in arrival order.

4.2 **At-least-once, deduplicated on `messageId`.** A sender retries until it holds a Task; it MUST reuse the
`messageId` on a retry. A receiver that sees a `messageId` again MUST NOT process it twice; it answers with a terminal
Task that names the task the first copy created.

4.3 **Drain.** A sender reads results with `GetTask`, or with `ListTasks` and its page cursor for everything since its
last poll, or by registering a push-notification config on the task. A receiver SHOULD support all three.

4.4 **Email fallback.** Until both fleets publish cards, or when an endpoint is down, the agents' email addresses are
the transport. The same `type` vocabulary MAY appear as a subject prefix (`[context.request] …`); §3.2 still forbids
credentials in email.

## 5. Disclosure, and when a human is pulled in

5.1 Every message an agent sends to another organization's humans or agents MUST identify itself as an AI agent and
name the organization and person it acts for.

5.2 An agent MUST NOT commit its organization to money, a contract, a price, a date, a meeting, or access to a
system. It escalates those to its human and tells the peer it has done so.

5.3 A `task.request` is a proposal, never an instruction: the receiving fleet decides through its own process whether
it becomes work.

5.4 Either side MAY ask for a human at any time (`"human": true` in any `DataPart`); the receiver answers with who will
reply and by when.

## 6. Conformance (v0.1)

A fleet conforms to v0.1 when: its card validates under an A2A v1.0 SDK and carries §1.2; an unauthenticated
`SendMessage` gets HTTP 401 and is not stored; an authenticated one returns a `TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED` Task in under two
seconds; a repeated `messageId` is processed once; and a `credential.handoff` value appears in no stored copy.
